editorial:
Imagine you are sitting on a train and look out the window, only to see someone getting murdered in a house across the tracks. That is exactly what happens to Miss Marple, a sweet older lady who is way sharper than she looks. She tells the police what she saw, but because there is no body and no evidence, they basically laugh her off. You will love how she does not let that stop her. She decides to play detective herself, using her knowledge of human nature to track down the truth. The whole movie has a cozy yet mysterious vibe that makes you feel like you are solving a puzzle right along with her.

You will really enjoy the acting here, as Miss Marple is funny and stubborn in the best way possible. The plot moves along well, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies. It is a great pick for a rainy afternoon. It is a charming ride that proves you should never underestimate a grandma with a magnifying glass.
endingExplained: Miss Marple eventually figures out that the murder did happen, but the killer tried to hide the body and fake everything. She uses her cleverness to trick the culprit into revealing themselves. In the end, the police realize she was right all along. The killer is caught and arrested, proving that her sharp eyes and patience were more effective than the official police investigation. Everything wraps up with the mystery solved and justice served.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic whodunits and strong female leads.
